==Biography==
After starting out on console systems primarily, Krepo's introduction to PC gaming was with Warcraft 3, and he eventually began playing World of Warcraft. After some time, Krepo discovered Defense of the Ancients - the game which ultimately led him to play League of Legends. Starting off at what he calls a “mediocre” level of play, Krepo improved his skill and his rank with the acquisition of a new computer.

===Season 1===
The first team Krepo played for was [[Fureur]]. He also spent a short time playing for [[La GG]] along with [[fredy122]] and [[Snoopeh]] among others, though the team was not a success. At the end of the season, Krepo joined [[Counter Logic Gaming Europe]] along with [[Wickd]], [[Snoopeh]], [[Froggen]], and [[Yellowpete]].

===Season 2===
Newly formed [[Counter Logic Gaming EU|CLG.EU]]'s first appearance would come at [[Kings of Europe]]. The team won the tournament and made a big statement by beating [[Moscow Five]] in the final. They would go on to follow this up with another triumph against Moscow Five, beating them in the final of the [[Corsair Vengeance Cup]].

A long season saw Krepo and CLG.EU face Moscow Five on a number of other occasions. The next time the two would meet was the final of [[DreamHack Summer 2012]], where again CLG.EU came out victorious. Despite their early season dominance, Froggen and the team were beaten by Moscow Five in the final of [[European Challenger Circuit: Poland|ECC Poland]].

Next up for CLG.EU were the [[Season 2/Regional Finals - Cologne|Regional Finals]], where the team placed 3rd behind [[SK Gaming]] and Moscow Five. The team's performance sealed them a spot at the [[Season 2 World Championship]]. In preparation for this, CLG.EU placed second at [[Azubu The Champions Summer 2012]] against mainly Korean opposition. 

At the [[Season 2 World Championship]], Krepo and the team finished in 2nd place in the group stages, securing them a place in the knockout rounds of the tournament. [[Counter Logic Gaming EU|CLG.EU]] beat [[Team WE]] in the quarterfinals of the tournament, but were beaten in the semifinals by [[Madlife]]'s [[Azubu Frost]].

The team finished the season off with a 3rd place finish at the [[2012 MLG Pro Circuit/Fall/Championship|MLG Fall Championship]] and a 2nd placed finish at [[DreamHack Winter 2012]]. At the close of the season, the team decided to split with the CLG organization and join [[Evil Geniuses.EU|Evil Geniuses]].

===Season 3===
A new challenge presented itself to Krepo and the team in the form of the upcoming [[Riot League Championship Series/Europe/Season 3/Spring Round Robin|LCS Spring Split]]. A number of good performances on {{ci|Thresh}} from Krepo saw the team finish 4th, granting them a spot in the [[Riot League Championship Series/Europe/Season 3/Spring Playoffs|Spring Playoffs]]. [[Evil Geniuses.EU|Evil Geniuses]] lost to [[Fnatic]] in the semifinals of the tournament, but the team clinched 3rd place by beating [[SK Gaming]] in the third-place match.

With Krepo now performing especially well on both {{ci|Thresh}} and {{ci|Sona}}, the [[Riot League Championship Series/Europe/Season 3/Summer Round Robin|Summer Split]] was strangely similar to the Spring Split for EG. With a 3rd place finish, they secured a spot in the [[Riot League Championship Series/Europe/Season 3/Summer Playoffs|Summer Playoffs]]. Playoffs losses to [[Fnatic]] in the semifinal and [[Moscow Five]] in the third-place match saw Evil Geniuses finish 4th.

At the end of the season, [[Evil Geniuses.EU|Evil Geniuses]] split into two parts, with [[Froggen]] and [[Wickd]] staying in Europe to form [[Alliance]], while Krepo, [[Snoopeh]], and [[Yellowpete]] stayed with the organization and moved to North America.

===2014 Season===
Krepo and the new team played in the [[Riot League Championship Series/North America/2014 Season/Spring Promotion|Spring Promotion]], acquiring the spot of [[Velocity eSports]]. Krepo and the team managed to beat [[To Be Determined]] to qualify for the [[Riot League Championship Series/North America/2014 Season/Spring Season|Spring Split]].

A disappointing 7th place finish in the regular season meant that Krepo and [[Evil Geniuses.NA|Evil Geniuses]] would be playing in the [[Riot_League_Championship_Series/North_America/2014_Season/Summer_Promotion|Summer Promotion]]. They were matched up with [[Cloud9 Tempest]] in the promotion tournament, and beat the team 3-1 to secure their place in the [[Riot League Championship Series/North America/2014 Season/Summer Season|Summer Split]]. 

Another below-par split saw Krepo and [[Evil Geniuses.NA|Evil Geniuses]] finish 7th in the regular season once again, meaning they would be playing in the [[Riot League Championship Series/North America/2015 Season/Spring Promotion|Spring Promotion]]. Here, Krepo and the team managed to beat [[Team Coast]] to qualify for the [[Riot League Championship Series/North America/2015 Season/Spring Season|Spring Season]]. However, Krepo left [[Evil Geniuses.NA|Evil Geniuses]] a month later.

===2015 Season===
At the start of the season, Krepo partnered with [[Cloud9]] as streamer.<ref>[http://www.facebook.com/Krepo.LoL/posts/802354739836760 Krepo's Facebook Post] ''facebook.com''</ref> A month later, he joined [[Elements]] to play in the [[Riot League Championship Series/Europe/2015 Season/Spring Season|Spring Season]] of the EU LCS, replacing [[Nyph]].<ref name="el krepo">[http://www.facebook.com/Krepo.LoL/posts/827628340642733 Krepo's Facebook post] ''facebook.com''</ref> Now reunited with [[Froggen]] and [[Wickd]], Krepo's contribution helped the team to a 7th place finish in the split, avoiding relegation. After the end of the split, Krepo announced his retirement.<ref>[http://www.facebook.com/Krepo.LoL/posts/859546400784260 Krepo's Facebook Post] ''facebook.com''</ref> 

Soon after his retirement, Krepo joined the EU LCS caster team for the start of the [[Riot League Championship Series/Europe/2015 Season/Summer Season|Summer Split]]<ref>[http://na.lolesports.com//articles/krepo-joins-eu-lcs-caster-team-2015-summer-split Krepo joins EU LCS caster team for 2015 Summer Split] ''lolesports.com''</ref> and subsequently was invited to be one of the Riot casters for the [[2015 Season World Championship|2015 Worlds]].

== Trivia ==
* Fan of good beer, especially the Belgian beer [http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duvel_Moortgat_Brewery Duvel].
* His favorite champion is {{ci|Blitzcrank}}, as stated on State of the League (June 21, 2012).
* Known for his strong {{ci|Leona}} gameplay in Season 2. 
* Occasionally refers to himself as "Scumbag (Skumbag) Krepo" when stealing kills from his AD carry.
* One of the first players in Europe to build full AP while supporting with champions like {{ci|Zyra}}.
* Played the AP carry role and mained {{ci|Anivia}} before switching to a support player. He has confirmed that he played about 1.5k games with Anivia in Season 1.
** He played mid-lane Anivia in an LCS game and won - namely the famous 2013 EU LCS Summer Split 3rd place tiebreaker game between Evil Geniuses and [[Gambit Gaming]] where Froggen played support {{ci|Blitzcrank}} in what became an EG blowout win. Krepo's K/D/A against [[Alex Ich]]'s {{ci|Twisted Fate}} was 5/1/6.
* Speaks French, English, Dutch and some German.
* Played with Yellowpete on team La GG
* Was part of the [[Season 3 World Championship]] analyst desk.<ref>[http://na.lolesports.com/articles/casters-and-analysts-announced-worlds Casters and analysts announced for Worlds] ''http://na.lolesports.com''</ref>
* Got his original name "Krepo" by "basically [...] slamming [his] hands on the keyboard".<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Be_FdzCpKKk#t=1m18s Closer Look: How You Got Your Name] ''http://youtube.com''</ref>
* Subbed in as support with [[Vander]] playing bot lane for [[FC Schalke 04 Esports]] in the first two games of the [[EU LCS/2018 Season/Spring Season|EU LCS 2018 Spring]], after bot laner [[Upset]] had a medical emergency and was unable to play.
* Subbed in as support for [[Steeelback]] on [[Vitality.Bee]] for one game during [[LFL 2020 Spring]] after he was promoted to the team's [[LEC 2020 Spring]] roster.
